fields.description:
## Problem

`infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` maintains hand-curated `*_PATHS` manifests (BOT_PATHS,
SECRETS_PATHS, MCP_PATHS, CONFIG_PATHS, EDGE_PATHS, MATERIALIZER_PATHS, OBS_PATHS,
CERTBOT_PATHS) that decide which merged file changes trigger a redeploy / detect-signal.
When a deploy-relevant infra file is ADDED but never listed, a subsequent change to it
drifts to the running environment silently. This exact class has recurred four times:
1d1b (nginx edge), 5524 (host-nginx materializers), 5d4c (mcp-entrypoint.sh, MCP_PATHS),
408c (materialize-deploy-key.sh, CONFIG_PATHS). Each was a manual list falling out of
sync with reality — a fail-OPEN omission that no test caught.

## Approach — derive-and-diff, NOT a second hand-list

Do not introduce a parallel curated "deploy-relevant files" list; that just relocates the
drift. Instead DERIVE the expected path set from sources already maintained for their own
reasons, and fail on drift. The enforced list becomes a *derived view* of a source of
truth, so it cannot silently drift.

In-repo precedent: `scripts/check_server_manifest.py` already does exactly this for
`server.json` — it derives the expected env-var records from the `rebar.mcp_server.MCP_ENV_VARS`
code inventory and "rejects missing names, extra names, changed fields". This guard is a
fourth sibling of that accepted pattern (cf. also `check_config_ownership.py`,
`check_verify_gate_parity.py`). OSS precedent for derive-from-reality vs a curated list:
`go mod tidy` + `git diff --exit-code`, Bazel Gazelle, Tinder `bazel-diff` (whose maintainers
warn a hand "approximate the affected set" yields "a system you can't trust"), Nx `affected`,
Pants `--changed-since`.

Derivation sources (independent of the manifest):
1. Dockerfile/compose directives — parse `infra/compose/Dockerfile.*` + `docker-compose.yml`
   for `COPY` / `install -m` / `ENTRYPOINT` script references (what is baked into the running
   images). Catches 5d4c (mcp-entrypoint.sh named in Dockerfile.mcp).
2. Filename conventions — glob `infra/**/materialize-*.sh`, `infra/**/*-entrypoint.sh`,
   `compose-up.sh`. Catches 408c + 5524 (materialize-*.sh).

### Parser resolution rule (Dockerfile/compose source A)

The Dockerfile/compose parser only accepts `COPY` / `install -m` / `ENTRYPOINT` (and compose
`entrypoint:`/`command:`) script references that RESOLVE TO AN EXISTING REPO FILE, and it
normalizes container paths to repo-relative POSIX paths first:
- a build-context path like `/app/infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh` has its `/app/` prefix
  stripped to the repo-relative `infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh`;
- an installed/container-absolute path like the ENTRYPOINT `/usr/local/bin/mcp-entrypoint.sh`
  is resolved by basename against the checkout's `infra/**`;
- a reference that resolves to NO repo file — a script GENERATED inside the image at build
  time (e.g. the heredoc-written `reviewbot-entrypoint.sh`) or an external binary — is
  discarded, not treated as a deploy-relevant repo path.
This keeps the derived set to real, in-repo, deploy-relevant source files.

### Coverage matching rule (mirror autodeploy's own semantics)

The check cross-references each derived path against the UNION of autodeploy.sh's `*_PATHS`.
Coverage is NOT exact string membership: it mirrors the git-pathspec matching autodeploy
itself uses. autodeploy decides "did a matching path change" with
`git -C "$MIRROR_DIR" diff --name-only <a> <b> -- $PATHS` (its `changed_range` at
autodeploy.sh:736), and several manifest entries are DIRECTORY prefixes (e.g. `src/rebar/`
with a trailing slash). So a derived path P counts as COVERED when ANY manifest entry T
(trailing slash ignored) satisfies `P == T` OR `P` is under directory `T` (`P` startswith
`T + "/"`) — the same prefix semantics git pathspec applies. Both sides are compared as
repo-relative POSIX paths. A derived path covered by NO manifest entry under this rule -> fail
(non-zero), printing the path and which derivation matched it.

## Fail-safe exclusion list

A small, commented exclusion list (in the check script) represents genuinely-intentional
exceptions. This is not optional polish: autodeploy.sh ALREADY documents a deliberate
exclusion (no AUTODEPLOY_PATHS block — self-update re-exec race, with a multi-line WHY), so
the guard MUST be able to encode "derived but intentionally not deploy-triggering". Each
excluded path carries an inline reason, and the guard verifies each exclusion still names a
real repo file (a stale exclusion is itself flagged). The guard thus OVER-flags (add the path
or annotate the exclusion) and never silently misses — the opposite failure mode from a bare
hand-list.

## Portability (project.portability)

Runs in-process via `make lint` as `python scripts/check_deploy_manifest.py`, mirroring the
~24 existing `scripts/check_*.py` guards. Stdlib only, no CI-provider trigger: any CI that
runs `make lint` enforces it, and the pre-commit hook runs it locally on `git commit`.
Portable to diverse-CI / no-CI environments.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `scripts/check_deploy_manifest.py` derives the expected path set from (a) Dockerfile/
      compose `COPY`/`install`/`ENTRYPOINT` script refs and (b) `materialize-*.sh` /
      `*-entrypoint.sh` / `compose-up.sh` globs under `infra/`.
- [x] The Dockerfile/compose parser only keeps script references that RESOLVE to an existing
      repo file, normalizing container prefixes (`/app/` stripped; installed-absolute paths
      resolved by basename) and DISCARDING build-artifact / image-generated paths.
- [x] It parses autodeploy.sh's `*_PATHS` (all `^[A-Z_]+_PATHS=` assignments) and exits
      non-zero when a derived path is in NONE of them, printing the path + matched source.
- [x] Coverage mirrors autodeploy's git-pathspec matching (its `changed_range`
      `git diff --name-only -- $PATHS`): a derived path counts as covered when ANY manifest
      entry is that path OR a directory prefix of it (trailing slash ignored), NOT exact
      string membership. A test pins this prefix semantics (e.g. `src/rebar/` covers
      `src/rebar/x.py`).
- [x] A commented exclusion list supports intentional exceptions; each excluded path has an
      inline reason and names a real repo file (encodes at least the documented
      install-autodeploy.sh-class exclusion).
- [x] A test asserts the derivation captures every historically-drifted recurrence class
      (mcp-entrypoint.sh, materialize-deploy-key.sh, materialize-*.sh, compose-up.sh,
      reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh), each with its matched derivation source.
- [x] Wired into the `make lint` target (not a standalone CI workflow), so it runs under the
      pre-commit hook and any CI that runs `make lint`.
- [x] RED->GREEN test: with a derived path removed from all manifests the check fails for the
      right reason; with manifests complete it passes. Mutation-checked (re-omit each covered
      path -> RED; restore).
- [x] Running the check against current `origin/main` PASSES (manifests are complete after
      f87719be9999).

## Out of scope

- No change to autodeploy runtime behaviour or apply/detect scope.
- Fully-dynamic deploy paths named by no convention and no Dockerfile/compose directive
  remain underivable — documented residual, handled by the exclusion list's fail-safe
  direction (a false negative there is no worse than today).

## File impact

- `scripts/check_deploy_manifest.py` (new)
- `Makefile` (add to the `lint` target)
- `tests/unit/test_check_deploy_manifest.py` (new)
- audited but NOT modified: `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh`, `infra/compose/Dockerfile.mcp`,
  `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml`
